lenses.lens: Detection-method SOTA: where the FDI + per-pixel MLP + Clay-fusion core sits vs the 7 reviewed method families
lenses.verdictOneLine: The detection CORE is a well-engineered instance of the cheap/older "spectral-index + classical ML" family (per-pixel MLP on hand-crafted indices, no spatial context); only the Clay ingredient is frontier-adjacent, and it functions as a frozen, zero-shot second-stage VERIFIER — a genuine precision-lift bolt-on, not a frontier detector — so the team's own "architectural/operational, not algorithmic novelty" positioning is honest and correct.
aheadOf: Orthogonal two-model fusion with a CALIBRATED CONFIRMED/POSSIBLE tier is operationally ahead of the review set: fusion_thresholds.json shows MLP-Plastic precision lifted 0.66->0.92 at 0.70 recall on held-out MARIDA+MADOS. Most reviewed papers report a single threshold and one accuracy number; explicit precision-recall trading for deployment is rare in the 25.

Reporting rigor exceeds much of the review: metrics.json discloses per-class precision/recall/F1 and a Water-inflated vs balanced macro-F1 separately, trained on 1.08M real MARIDA+MADOS pixels. Several reviewed works report only site accuracy or single-region results.

It is one of only two entries in the review moving toward geospatial foundation models at all (the other being Dalsasso CSM-Debris). Using Clay v1.5 embeddings + kNN retrieval + novelty puts the system in the 2024-era FM direction while most of the field is still spectral-index or CNN.

They attempted real external validation (Plastic Litter Project HDPE + wood control), which the review notes is rarely done. Even though it exposed weakness, the wood-control result is a genuine win: 5/15 MLP false-plastic calls were all correctly downgraded to POSSIBLE by the fusion.

Deployment realism the pure-research papers lack: pluggable ONNX with an interpretable FDI+NDVI+brightness heuristic fallback, and best-effort Clay so a sidecar outage degrades gracefully to MLP-only rather than breaking the scan.
behindOn: The detector itself is not frontier. A per-pixel MLP over 11 hand-engineered spectral indices (inference_engine._features) is methodologically the SAME family as Biermann/Sannigrahi/Nivedita's spectral-index + RF/SVM/NB — arguably simpler, since it has zero spatial/texture context. This is the cheap/older end of the taxonomy, not U-Net segmentation, YOLO detection, or hyperspectral material ID.

Held-out Plastic precision is only 0.66, and on the ONLY real external target (PLP HDPE) recall was 2/21 with Clay plastic-affinity 0.0 — the system essentially failed to detect real floating plastic. No externally validated field-accuracy figure is claimable (the team admits this), which is the honest but damning detection-SOTA verdict.

Clay is a FROZEN, off-the-shelf general Earth-observation FM used zero-shot, not the debris-specific self-supervised cross-sensor pretraining Dalsasso demonstrates (+~20% F1/IoU on transfer). Clay's OWN plastic F1 is 0.37 (precision 0.27) and its novelty separation (in-dist 0.123 vs new-seas 0.150, gap 0.028) is near-zero — so the 'generalises to new seas' claim is thinly supported by the team's own clay_analytics.json. It cannot detect plastic; it can only gate candidates.

They built a patch CNN (marinenet_patch.onnx) and it LOST to the per-pixel MLP due to scene scarcity, so on the CNN/U-Net axis they are behind-by-necessity, not competitive. This mirrors MARIDA's RF>U-Net but means no segmentation-quality spatial output.

No hyperspectral material/polymer ID and no optical+SAR fusion — two of the reviewed frontiers are entirely absent. This is sensor-bound (Sentinel-2 10-20 m multispectral) and not fixable within the current design, but under a strict detection-SOTA lens it is still a gap.
lenses.mostImportantGap: Promote Clay from a frozen second-stage verifier to a first-class detector, or stop implying detection-method novelty. Right now the frontier ingredient does the least detecting: its plastic F1 is 0.37 and its novelty signal barely separates (0.028). To actually reach the Dalsasso foundation-model frontier the team would need to fine-tune / LoRA-adapt Clay on MARIDA+MADOS debris (or use its dense patch tokens for segmentation) so it contributes detection recall — not just a hand-tuned kNN affinity gate over candidates the spectral MLP already produced. Absent that, the correct and defensible framing is exactly the one the team already uses: the contribution is architectural, operational, and transparency, NOT detection-method advancement.

lenses.verdictOneLine: Rigorous data-provenance and unusually honest self-testing, undermined by a Water-dominated "98.9%" headline, a failing in-situ result that isn't led with, and a demo that often runs an unvalidated heuristic — so no accuracy or ETA claim can currently stand.
aheadOf: The team actually ran a real in-situ validation the reviewed high-number papers mostly didn't: PLP 2021 (Topouzelis/Aegean) deployed HDPE targets WITH a wood control (models/plp_clay_validation.json). A deployed-target + natural-material-control design is more scientifically honest than Biermann-86% / Sannigrahi-91% headline figures taken on curated scenes.

Generalization is actually measured, not assumed: the RFO (Russwurm 2023) held-out new-seas experiment quantifies cross-domain debris recall (Clay 0.542 vs pp11 0.222 at 7.6% water FP), and the RFO-augmented model was NOT promoted because it lost the primary benchmark (0.767 vs 0.787) — most reviewed papers report only in-domain numbers and hide the transfer cliff.

Calibration discipline: the fusion stage ships an explicit operating point (confirmedPrecision 0.9219 / confirmedRecall 0.7037) with named thresholds (conf_high 0.7, aff_min 0.1, anomaly_tau 0.2) tuned to a stated target precision (0.92), versus the single hand-set FDI threshold (~0.02) typical of the index+ML literature.

Clean data provenance and reproducibility hygiene: official MARIDA+MADOS train/val/test splits (Kikaki 2022/2024), ONNX-vs-training agreement 1.0, prior models retained (marinenet_prev/pp7/patch/rfo) for auditability — stronger experimental record-keeping than most of the 25 reviewed works.
Per-stage live-vs-demo tagging and open disclosure of synthetic components directly addresses the review's named field gap (e), deployment transparency — which none of the reviewed systems claim.

Drift is more real than the brief states: the code attempts REAL Open-Meteo currents/winds keyless and gridded CMEMS/ERA5 forcing (trajectory/forecast.py, gridded_forcing.py) with synthetic only as fallback — the physics path exists, matching DEEP-PLAST's real-forcing ambition.
behindOn: The ONE real in-situ test is effectively a failing grade and is not led with: on PLP deployed HDPE targets the MLP calls only 2/21 'Plastic' (hdpeHitRate 0.333) and misclassifies 80% of the wood control as plastic (woodAsPlasticRate 0.80); Clay plastic-affinity is 0.00 for every target and NOTHING is CONFIRMED. Against Biermann 86%, Sannigrahi 91%, Nivedita 87.25% (real scenes), the Tracker has no defensible real-world detection number — its only field test says the pipeline misses two-thirds of deployed plastic and confuses natural driftwood for it.

The headline '98.9% accuracy / 0.79 macro-F1' is scientifically misleading: accuracy is dominated by the Water class (F1 0.995, ~97% of pixels), while Plastic/Algae/Sea-Foam precision is only 0.66/0.61/0.61 — i.e. the confounder-robustness the review flags as the field's core weakness is exactly where this model is weakest, and the big number hides it.

The product demo often runs the interpretable FDI+NDVI+brightness heuristic, not the validated MLP — so the accuracy/precision figures quoted anywhere in the console have NO validated number behind what the user is actually watching. The transparency contribution collapses if the demoed detector is the one component with zero reported accuracy.

Drift ETA has zero validation against real drifter/GPS tracks, and the demo path falls back to a synthetic current/wind field; time-to-coast ETAs are therefore uncalibrated. DEEP-PLAST at least forced on real Copernicus/NOAA fields (even if drift validation was only qualitative) — the Tracker cannot yet even claim that.

Target region has no supporting evidence: INCOIS/NCCR/Indian-Coast-Guard deployment is claimed for the Indian Ocean, yet every accuracy number is from Mediterranean/global MARIDA+MADOS/PLP, and cross-domain recall on unseen seas drops to 0.22–0.41. Nivedita's 87.25% on REAL Indian coastal waters exists in the literature; the Tracker has no Indian in-situ point, no Indian scene benchmark, and no domain-adaptation result there.

A legacy 'synthetic Sentinel-2 spectral library' descriptor still sits in metrics.json (line 90) alongside the real-data model card — a provenance-labeling inconsistency that, for a system whose headline contribution is transparency, is a self-inflicted credibility wound.
lenses.mostImportantGap: Retire the 98.9% headline and never surface an accuracy or ETA figure that isn't (a) produced by the model actually running in that view and (b) validated on the relevant distribution. Concretely: make the demo run the validated MLP (not the heuristic) or clearly label heuristic output as un-benchmarked; lead every accuracy claim with macro-F1 0.787 AND the PLP in-situ result (33% HDPE hit rate, 80% wood-as-plastic) rather than the Water-inflated accuracy; and gate every drift ETA behind an explicit 'not validated against real drifter tracks' caveat until at least one track comparison exists. The honest negative in-situ number must be the flagship figure — it is the team's most credible scientific asset and currently the most buried.

lenses.lens: Operational / Deployment / Product — is the end-to-end agency-facing console a real, defensible differentiator vs single-method benchmark papers (esp. DEEP-PLAST), and what would INCOIS/Coast Guard still need?
aheadOf: It is the only END-TO-END DEPLOYABLE PRODUCT in the comparison set. Every one of the 25 reviewed papers (Biermann, Sannigrahi, MARIDA/RF, MAP-Mapper, CSM-Debris, even DEEP-PLAST) is a single-method benchmark study that stops at an accuracy table. The Tracker delivers detection→DBSCAN cluster→drift→alert→ops-board→mission-report→active-learning as one running system with a React operations console, WebSocket live feed, and REST API. Nothing in the review ships a usable operator workflow.

Per-stage LIVE-vs-DEMO transparency is genuinely operationalized, not just claimed. The review's own Table III names deployment transparency (gap e) as rarely disclosed across the whole field; this system tags provenance per stage (X-Data-Source header, provider:demo labels, DEMO-suffixed scene IDs, engineOffline returning EMPTY results rather than fabricated ones). This is the paper's stated contribution and it is real in the code — a defensible differentiator no reviewed paper matches.

A closed human-in-the-loop feedback loop exists as product, not slideware: analyst confirm/false-alarm labels + uncertainty-sampled review queue → export to retrain (active learning). No reviewed paper — including DEEP-PLAST — delivers an operator labeling loop wired to model improvement.

Agency-shaped operational scaffolding is present: RBAC (Admin/Coastguard/Field/Ministry) enforced server-side, field-ops task lifecycle (PLANNED→DISPATCHED→IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED with event timeline), filed mission-report dossiers, and an advisory 'complements, never replaces patrols' DISCLAIMER printed on every CSV/PDF export. This is the workflow an INCOIS/ICG desk actually lives in; benchmark papers have no concept of it.

Real operational engineering discipline: graceful degradation everywhere with LABELED fallbacks (Prisma→mock, engine-offline→empty-not-fake), a BullMQ queue+worker decoupling the API from the ~7-60s scan, bounded caches that never fabricate, and honest metric badges (the previously fabricated ResNet f1Score:0.872 was replaced with the real held-out macro-F1). This is a maturity level the reviewed literature never has to demonstrate.

Ingest and drift are more 'live' than a pure benchmark: Sentinel-2 discovery is keyless via Element84 STAC, pixel reflectance is real CDSE/Sentinel Hub with SCL cloud/land masking, AND drift is forced by REAL keyless Open-Meteo hourly currents+winds (the briefing under-credited this as synthetic; synthetic sinusoidal is only the labeled fallback). So the operational drift product runs on real met-ocean data, closer to DEEP-PLAST's real-forcing setup than any other reviewed work.
behindOn: It cannot actually be stood up on agency infrastructure today. Infra is single-node localhost (bundled pgdata/redis, watchdog.ps1, install-scheduled-tasks.ps1) with NO IaC, NO HTTPS/WSS, dev JWT secrets, real API credentials sitting in .env, and — critically — WRITE ROUTES ARE PUBLIC (auth wired but not enforced on writes). Zero automated tests exist (vitest/pytest configured, none written). Production-readiness self-scored 6/10, security 5/10. An agency IT team could not deploy or accept this as-is; it is a demonstrator, not a pilot install.

No operational trust basis for dispatch decisions. Marine-Debris (Plastic) precision is ~0.36 on the held-out combined MARIDA+MADOS test (recall high, macro-F1 ~0.50; the 0.79 macro-F1 in the briefing looks like a more favorable/older split — the shipped metrics.json shows 0.500 combined). ~2 of every 3 flagged 'plastic' pixels are false positives, and confidence is uncalibrated for Indian-Ocean water. A Coast Guard team dispatching patrols on that hit rate burns fuel and trust. There is NO independent (non-MARIDA/MADOS) Indian-Ocean field validation — exactly the review's Table III gap (b) it aspires to fill.

Quantitative-integrity landmine for agency reporting: detection area is a pseudo-quantity (_area_from_fdi inflates a 10m pixel's true 0.0001 km² by ~1000×) and it flows into dashboard sums and CSV/PDF exports, caveated only in an explain-drawer. Any INCOIS/NCCR situation report built on summed area would be off by three orders of magnitude — a credibility-killer the moment a domain reviewer checks it.

Drift forecasting — the operational headline feature — is thinly built and unvalidated. Forcing is a release-point time series (not a gridded field sampled along the path), the coast ETA is a crude longitude-crossing check, forcing is Open-Meteo not the agency-standard CMEMS currents + ERA5 winds, and there is NO validation against real drifter/GPS tracks. DEEP-PLAST (real Copernicus currents + NOAA winds, integrated F1 0.84) is at least at parity on forcing and ahead on integrated detection; both share qualitative drift validation, so the Tracker has no operational edge here and a weaker detector feeding it.

Optical-only, so it is blind exactly when the Indian coast needs it most. Sentinel-2's ~5-day revisit + monsoon cloud cover means multi-week detection blackouts over the peak-debris season. The review repeatedly flags SAR/multi-modal for all-weather coverage; the system ingests no Sentinel-1. For an operational Indian-Ocean tool this is a coverage gap an agency would notice in the first monsoon.

The 'agency-facing' loop stops at the console edge. There is no real outbound alert channel an operations center uses (no email/SMS/INCOIS-bulletin or ICG C2 integration — alerts live in-app), no multi-user concurrency/load testing, no audit trail or data-retention/governance layer, and no calibrated uncertainty on any number an officer would act on. The workflow is well-modeled but not yet connected to how an agency is actually notified and held accountable.
lenses.mostImportantGap: Convert the localhost demonstrator into something an agency could actually trial: (1) a hardened hosted deployment — enforce auth on write routes, HTTPS/WSS, rotate the .env credentials, add a smoke-test suite; (2) ONE independent (non-MARIDA/MADOS) Indian-Ocean validation scene with published precision/recall so a Coast Guard officer has a real hit-rate to trust; and (3) fix the ~1000× area pseudo-quantity before it reaches any exported report. Without these three, the impressive end-to-end console remains a demo — the product differentiator is real, but it is currently undeployable, untrusted, and quantitatively unsafe for the agencies it targets.
lenses.verdictOneLine: Genuinely the only deployable, transparent, agency-shaped PRODUCT in a field of single-method benchmarks — a real and defensible operational differentiator — but today it is a hardened-demo away from a pilot: undeployable on agency infra, unvalidated on real hit-rate, and carrying a 1000x area error into its own reports.
